author: TEDx Talks
description:
In times of war, survival becomes the priority - and everything else fades into the background. But what happens after survival?

In this TEDx talk, Youth Development Specialist Nana Fredua Agyeman explores why rebuilding a nation requires more than recovery. Using Ukraine as a case study, he highlights the urgent need to invest in young people as the foundation for long-term renewal and stability.

Because the future of a country is not only shaped on the battlefield, but in the generations that follow. Nana Fredua Agyeman is a Youth Development Specialist working at the intersection of youth employment, social protection and digital transformation. He supports governments and partners across the Young World countries to design and scale technology-enabled systems that expand pathways to work for young people and strengthen safety nets for vulnerable populations. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Le
title: Young people are leaving Ukraine—why it matters | Nana Fredua Agyeman | TEDxUniversity of Essex

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Women and girls are significantly less likely to be diagnosed with ADHD than their male counterparts. Instead, they're labeled "difficult," "disorganized," and "dramatic"— labels that perpetuate misunderstanding and stand in the way of their success. Melanie spent three decades leading in the nonprofit sector, public service, and politics before getting her own diagnosis as an adult. She argues that naming it was liberating, not limiting. As a former cabinet minister and mother to a daughter with ADHD, she shares how the traits often dismissed as weaknesses became the foundation of her leadership, and offers practical ways to support neurodivergent women so they can thrive.
 HLI HAYKWHL ẂII XSGAAK, Melanie Mark is a trailblazing Nisga'a, Gitxsan, Cree and Ojibway matriarch and the first First Nations woman to be elected to the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia in 2016. She is also the inaugural First Nations woman to serve in BC’s Cabinet as the Minister of Advanced Education,
title: How my ADHD diagnosis liberated me | Melanie Mark | TEDxWest Vancouver Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The hardest thing to rebuild after a major life change isn't a routine, it's a sense of self. In her talk, Fei posits that these moments of upheaval, as disorienting as they feel, are an invitation to rediscover who you are still becoming.
 Fei is a professional life coach who works with individuals navigating life's major transitions: mothers, teenagers, couples, and anyone rebuilding a sense of purpose after change. She is also a content creator whose videos have found a wide audience drawn to her message of continued growth, reinvention, and staying connected to oneself. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to Rediscover Yourself When Life Forces You to Start Over  | Fei Ma | TEDxWest Vancouver Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Victoria Pippo argues that burnout isn't caused by working too much, it's caused by days that have no structure, no rhythm, and no deliberate pause. In this talk, she introduces 'Energy Punctuation', a four-part framework for moving through demanding days with greater clarity and capacity, without dismantling the life you've built.
 Victoria Pippo is a leadership mentor and speaker who works with high-performing women navigating burnout, pressure, and emotional overload. Drawing from her background in performance and leadership coaching, she brings a practitioner's understanding of what it actually takes to build sustainable rhythms without sacrificing ambition or responsibility. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to take a pause every day | Victoria Pippo | TEDxWest Vancouver Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Communities don’t fall apart because people disagree. They fall apart because people stop participating. In this talk, David Huff introduces the idea of “trail magic”—small, timely acts of help—and shows how they form the foundation of strong communities. Drawing from experiences on the Appalachian Trail and beyond, he makes a simple case: when we step in instead of stepping back, we become part of what makes things work. "David Huff is a strategist, photographer, and conservationist based in Asheville, North Carolina. He is the founder of Corporate Craft, a consulting practice that helps leaders and organizations navigate complexity with clarity, alignment, and shared purpose. He also founded the George Masa Foundation, which inspires young people to engage with and protect the natural world through photography and storytelling.

David serves on the board of the Blue Ridge Parkway Foundation and is an active member of the Carolina Mountain Club, where he maintains a section of the Ap
title: We are trail magic: What the trail teaches us about showing up | David Huff | TEDxAsheville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sometimes, before plants die, they’ve already been trying to speak. But we’re the ones who can’t hear them yet.

In his work, Malikul Ikram demonstrates how plants send chemical signals and how to interpret them through metabolomics. Through the story of a dying tree and examples of tomatoes and pineapples whose flavors change according to their water needs and biological processes, he shows that every flavor, color, and resilience of fruits and plants actually stems from a hidden chemical conversation.
 A biotechnology researcher and co-founder of BIOPS Agrotek dedicated to advancing Indonesia’s agricultural commodities. He pioneered an automated irrigation algorithm for horticulture and broadened his metabolomics research to unlock the full potential of local agricultural products. Through these innovations, he champions smarter, more efficient, and more sustainable agricultural practices that create lasting impact. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format
title: Metabolomic: Decrypting the Secret Language of Nature | MM. Malikul Ikram  | TEDxBandung

description:
You have an intelligence you may not be using—one that guides you in living a life true to your deepest self. Imaginative intelligence is the realm of creativity, intuition, humor, awe, aesthetic appreciation, and insight. Allegra Huston explores how this non-rational intelligence works, why we tend to ignore it, and how reconnecting with it builds creativity, courage, and alignment with what you hold precious. "Allegra Huston is a pioneer of ""imaginative intelligence"": the inner network, fueled by imagination, that generates our sense of self. In an era when AI has created a crisis of intelligence, Allegra argues that our most valuable personal intelligence is based not on logic and knowledge, but on our uniquely human capacities of imagination, awe, aesthetic appreciation, and intuition.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when the dreams we carry for ourselves are shaped by the expectations of others?
In this talk, Muhammad Zeeshan Mirza shares a deeply personal story about wanting to become a fiction writer, while being guided toward a more stable academic path that eventually led him to complete a PhD. Rather than focusing on regret or failure, the talk explores how decisions are often influenced by family, culture, responsibility, and collective values.
Drawing from experiences common across many Asian societies, the speaker reflects on the difference between individual and collective decision-making — and why one should not be seen as superior to the other.
This talk invites the audience to rethink what it means to choose a path in life, and reminds us that there is no single “correct” way to make decisions. What truly matters is the understanding, courage, and responsibility behind them. Dr. Muhammad Zeeshan Mirza completed his PhD in 2019 and was later awarded the Doctor of Sciences
title: The story I wasn't allowed to write - and why that matters  | Dr. Muhammad Zeeshan Mirza | TEDxNewUU

description:
What if the best investment you ever made cost nothing but a 20-minute detour?

In this candid and compelling talk, Ria (Saroni) Ghosh, takes us back to her first weeks in Bombay as a young professional navigating a city of 20 million strangers. Through a story involving a flooded apartment, a floating mattress, and one neighbor who showed up when it mattered most, she traces it all back to a single act of spontaneous kindness weeks earlier.

Ria makes a quietly powerful case that in a world optimized for productivity and distraction, the most valuable thing you can offer is your undivided attention. Not your resume, not your title, but the simple willingness to look up and notice someone else's struggle.

Because when the floods come, your accolades cannot hold a mop. Only people can do that. Saroni Ghosh is a Go-To-Market Lead at Google in the United States, where she works on work tracking, planning, and assistance solutions. With over 14 years of experience across media, FMCG, rea

En esta charla, Andrea Ochoa, estudiante de Nutrición y promotora del bienestar integrativo, nos invita a replantear la forma en que entendemos la salud y la relación con la comida. A partir de su historia personal y del llamado “misterio de Roseto”, Andrea nos muestra que la nutrición va más allá de contar calorías: incluye los alimentos del plato y también los que no se ven, como las relaciones, el descanso, el propósito y la conexión emocional. 
Una charla íntima y reveladora que nos recuerda que la salud no es un destino, sino un camino que se vive en balance todos los días.
 Estudiante de la Licenciatura en Nutrición y Ciencia de los Alimentos en la Universidad
Iberoamericana, Tijuana. Cuenta con una certificación en Salud Integrativa por
el Instituto de Nutrición Integrativa de Nueva York (IIN), avalada por organizaciones
(NBHWC, ICF, Chopra Global, NASM) lo que le permite abordar la salud desde una
perspectiva holística y personalizada.
A través de su cuenta de Instagram (@andy
title: El menú invisible de la salud | Andrea Ochoa Martínez | TEDxTecate Youth

Sometimes the most honest voices emerge from the land where we first learned to speak our own names.

Minanto revives the pulse of Indramayu through his book "Kemelut Rondasih dan Dua Anaknya" (The Turmoil of Rondasih and Her Two Children). He explores how village stories, local sayings, and ever-changing landscapes shape the way a person views the world and understands themselves. We are invited to see that identity is not merely a place of birth, but a space where tradition, experience, and social consciousness intersect and sharpen one another, making it a mirror through which to reexamine the meaning of home, origin, and what it means to be human. A writer from Indramayu, best known for the novel Aib dan Nasib, which won the 2019 Jakarta Arts Council Novel Competition and was included in Tempo’s 2020 Prose Choice. He also teaches writing classes in his hometown, believing that literature is not merely for enjoyment, but a meaningful way to preserve tradition and culture. This talk
title: Investigating the Unspoken Truth through Fictioning | Minanto  | TEDxBandung

description:
Wounds are not the enemy; they are a small corner within ourselves that must be seen, heard, and ultimately embraced.

Zaky Yamani shares how childhood wounds, fear, and darkness that had been buried for years eventually erupted, causing him to lose his footing. In the long journey toward healing, fiction became a space to mend his own wounds, while his nonfiction and activism in the field of human rights became a way to tend to the wounds of others. Every piece he writes and every voice he champions demonstrates that darkness can be transformed into a torch.
 A writer and human rights activist with several novels and short story collections to his name, including the trilogy Perjalanan Mustahil Samiam dari Lisboa, written during his residency in Portugal, and the nationally acclaimed Kereta Semar Lembu. He currently serves as a Campaigner for Amnesty International Indonesia, championing human rights and meaningful social change. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED confe
title: The Power of Embracing Trauma: Turning Pain into Purpose | Zaky Yamani  | TEDxBandung

Being twins is often seen as cute, unique, or intriguing, yet there is actually a much deeper psychological experience behind it.

Through lighthearted personal stories and accounts from the Twins Universe community, Eva Sri Rahayu and Evi Sri Rezeki invite us to see that the anxiety of being compared by those around us is not experienced only by twins, but by many people. Some of us grow up under the weight of others’ expectations, assumptions, and narratives, to the point where we forget to see ourselves as individuals. They demonstrate how creative work and community spaces can serve as safe havens for discovering one’s voice, identity, and true self.
 Eva Sri Rahayu and Evi Sri Rezeki are twin writers who work across various forms of production, ranging from novels and essays to children’s literature and audiovisual works. title: Reclaiming One's Identity in a World of Comparison | Eva Sri Rahayu  & Evi Sri Rejeki  | TEDxBandung

Curiosity is not a personality trait. It is a discipline, one that can shape careers, companies, institutions, and the future itself.

In this TEDx talk, Ron Shlien shares how a childhood experiment at age 13 helped spark the creation of Mad Science, a global STEM education brand, and later influenced his work as Canada’s first Entrepreneur-in-Residence.

Through personal stories and reflections on education, entrepreneurship, innovation, and AI, Ron argues that the future will not belong only to those with the fastest answers, but to those who keep asking better questions.
 A visionary entrepreneur and co-founder of Mad Science, a leader in children’s STEM education, Ron Shlien has spent over 40 years designing innovative learning experiences that have inspired millions of young people across 29 countries.?

If extinction is inevitable, what would it mean to design it ethically? Aroussiak Gabrielian confronts modern design’s obsession with stability, control, and permanence. Through rivers, maps, breath, and the human body itself, she reveals how we freeze living systems into simplified images — and then wonder why they fail. Moving between ecological science, ancestral knowledge, and speculative prototypes, she reframes design as metabolic participation — an ongoing exchange within systems that exceed us. Her provocation is both unsettling and urgent: the future of design is not about preservation at all costs — but about learning how to participate responsibly in cycles that will outlast us.
